lead: Burlington plumbing deals with long cold winters, old homes on the hill and lake-effect snow. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Burlington.
risk: frozen pipes, aging pipes in old homes and boiler and heating issues
risk_short: frozen pipes, old pipes and boilers
why: The Old North End, the Hill Section and the South End have homes from the 1850s to the 1930s, many split into apartments. Galvanized supply lines, cast-iron stacks and old sewer laterals are common.
Long, cold winters freeze pipes near exterior walls. Many homes use boilers, so heating and plumbing problems overlap.
water: Burlington treats water from Lake Champlain. It is soft to moderately hard.
problems: Old North End and the Hill Section
tips: Keep the heat on in every unit through winter.
Have your boiler serviced before winter.
Know where each unit's shutoff is.
areas: PipeMend works Downtown and in the Old North End, the Hill Section, the South End, the New North End and every other Burlington neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the Burlington Department of Permitting and Inspections, and plumbers are licensed through the Vermont Division of Fire Safety.

faq.a: Vermont licenses plumbers through the Division of Fire Safety. Permits for work in Burlington come from the city's Department of Permitting and Inspections.
